summary: Clarify which dashboards/alerts define 'overload shedding' vs incident-worthy internal errors for oncall paging
description:
Request from oncall + internal support: we need a single, explicit definition of what should page vs what should be treated as expected/managed load shedding.

Context
- With Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding rolling out, we are seeing higher volumes of 429/503 that are "expected" during overload (and should not page as hard failures), while still needing to page on true internal failures (routing/control-plane issues, runtime crashes, gateway errors not attributable to shedding).
- Current confusion: different dashboards/alerts are being used interchangeably across teams, resulting in either missed incidents (internal 5xx hidden by aggregate error rate) or noisy paging (shed events treated like outages).

What we need
1) Canonical dashboards for overload triage vs incident triage:
   - Overload triage dashboard: breaker state + shed rate + queue depth + capacity signals.
   - Incident triage dashboard: internal error breakdown excluding overload-protected errors.

2) Canonical paging policy:
   - Which alerts page oncall (P0/P1) vs ticket-only.
   - Explicit thresholds/windows and labels.

3) SLO/error budget accounting guidance:
   - Confirm that overload-protected errors (Redwood overload codes + HTTP mapping) are tracked separately from internal 5xx for SLO burn.

4) Runbook update:
   - Add a short section at top of Hosted overload mitigation runbook: "Is this overload shedding or internal failure?" with decision tree + the 3–5 links we should always use.

Impact
- Oncall currently has inconsistent behavior across rotations; risk of retry storms + delayed response when control plane is unhealthy.
- Support responders are unsure what to tell internal stakeholders during spikes ("is this expected shedding or are we down?").

Links / references
- Slack: #eng-oncall thread on paging rules + SLO accounting (thread-1720875501)
- Slack: #eng-sre dashboard review + alert thresholds (thread-1720948820)
- Slack: #eng-oncall playbook update discussion (thread-1722098811)
- Confluence: hosted-api-overload-slos-and-error-budget-policy.json
- Confluence: overload-protection-dashboards.json
- Confluence: hosted-overload-mitigation-runbook.json

Acceptance criteria
- One Confluence snippet (or section) clearly states paging policy + links to canonical dashboards.
- Alert definitions updated so load shedding doesn’t trigger paging by itself.
- Oncall runbook updated with a decision tree and "known good" Grafana links.
- Confirmed in #eng-oncall that policy is understood and in effect.

Owner request
- Primary: Observability/SRE (Aisha + Sergio)
- Review: Rafael Mendes (SRE lead), Allison Grant (metrics standards), Mina Haddad (routing), Amara Diallo (gateway).
comments: 2025-12-09 10:22 Owen Phillips (reporter): We got paged twice last week during a traffic spike where everything was shedding correctly. We also had one case where routing was unhealthy but it looked similar in aggregate error rate. Need a clean split between "managed overload" and "internal failure" and to align alerts.

2025-12-09 11:05 Aisha Bello (assignee): Ack. I’ll draft a simple decision tree + propose alert routing changes. Can someone confirm the intended accounting: overload-protected errors should not burn availability SLO, correct?

2025-12-09 11:18 Rafael Mendes: Correct direction. Overload-protected errors (standard overload codes + Retry-After) should be accounted separately from internal 5xx. But we still need guardrails: if shed rate is high AND breaker open persists beyond expected recovery windows, we should page as capacity/regional issue (but different severity).

2025-12-10 09:41 Sergio Costa: For dashboards, proposing two canonical links: (1) "Overload Protection" dashboard (breaker state, queue, shed reasons, p99) and (2) "Hosted API - Internal Errors" dashboard (5xx excluding overload-protected). Will add a panel that explicitly shows error mix: overload-protected vs internal-fault vs client-throttle.

2025-12-10 13:27 Allison Grant: Please ensure metric labels don’t explode (model + region + tier is OK; tenant_id is not). Also, define the exact filter for overload-protected errors (error_code prefix + http_status mapping) so it’s consistent across gateway/routing/runtime.

2025-12-11 16:02 Aisha Bello: Draft paging policy:
- Page P1 when "internal-fault" error rate > threshold (per region) for 10m OR control-plane health SLI fails.
- Do NOT page on overload-protected 429/503 alone.
- Create ticket (no page) when shed rate > X% for 15m OR breaker remains open for >Y min; page only if accompanied by elevated internal faults OR multi-region impact.
Will post to #eng-oncall for review.

2025-12-12 09:08 Owen Phillips: +1. Please also clarify how streaming disconnects map: if disconnect reason is overload-protected (explicit reason), no page; if gateway 5xx/stream-reset without overload code, treat as internal-fault and page.

2025-12-13 14:44 Aisha Bello: Updated runbook section "Is this overload or an incident?" with:
1) Check internal-fault vs overload-protected ratio.
2) If overload-protected dominates, consult breaker state + capacity; consider comms + rate shaping.
3) If internal-fault dominates or control plane errors spike, treat as incident.
Added links to canonical dashboards.
Requesting signoff from Rafael + Sergio.

2025-12-16 10:11 Rafael Mendes: Approved. Key point: breaker open is not itself an incident; persistent breaker open with increasing internal-faults or inability to recover is incident. Please ensure alert titles reflect this to reduce confusion.

2025-12-16 17:02 Aisha Bello: Implemented alert changes in Grafana alert rules + updated Hosted overload mitigation runbook. Posted summary in #eng-oncall with links + decision tree. Marking resolved.
resolution: Defined canonical dashboards and paging policy separating overload-protected (managed shedding) vs internal-fault errors; updated alert rules to avoid paging on load shedding alone; added a decision tree + dashboard links to Hosted overload mitigation runbook; communicated and confirmed in #eng-oncall.
